newsitem.title: UK: GUS eyes Freemans but fears monopoly probe.
newsitem.headline: GUS eyes Freemans but fears monopoly probe.

text.p: Home shopping group Great Universal Stores Plc said it would be interested in buying Freemans catalogue business, just put up for sale by Sears Plc, but fears this would be subject to a monopoly investigation.
Chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale told a news conference, "Clearly GUS would have to say it is interested in the possibility of acquiring another UK mail order company."

But he said as the largest player in the UK market already it would probably be subject to a Monopolies and Mergers Commission referral, making it a less desirable buyer from Sears point of view. "We do have a handicap," he said.
On Monday, Sears confirmed it was in talks to sell its catalogue business, the third largest in the UK.
Privately-owned retailer Littlewoods has been tipped as a likely buyer, along with German home shopping group Otto Versand and France's La Redoute, owned by Pinault-Printemps-Redoute.
Freemans is estimated to be worth around 400 million pounds.
GUS's catalogues, which sell via agents, include Kays, Great Universal and Marshall Ward.
